sourceText: On night 18, the course began with a prohibition: no one was allowed to solve the problem before they could describe who would pay for the solution. Only then did Aster open the DIMENSIONAL-WOUND sector. A solar system has been locally reduced from three dimensions to two, and the planets have become maps of their own interiors. The memorial bore the name of Liu Cixin; dimensional-war traditions precisely to keep the genealogy of the idea visible. Aster considered it indecent for a late civilization to treat the imagination of the past as anonymous ore: authors did not own the futures, but they deserved to remain on the map as points of intellectual origin. The children had quickly learned that a wormhole is also a trade treaty, and an additional dimension is also a method for walking through prison walls. Kesh built his classifications as instruments of falsification: a good category had to state what it did not cover, not merely what it could absorb. The children were met by Orel, who refused demonstrations. ‘If you can perform miracles, perform them after you tell me what becomes irreversible.’ Marae appreciated the formulation; Aster 109 admitted that in earlier eras she herself would have asked the question only after optimizing. The problem closed quickly around them: Digital copies of the victims reject “restoration” to three dimensions, regarding it as the creation of successors rather than their own return. There was no clean option. Every intervention shifted the cost between persons, eras, or definitions of personhood; and refusing to intervene was itself a choice made by those who could leave. Kesh opened the analytical layer of the Table for a few seconds. The active cells were Dp — Additional Dimensions: space has more degrees of freedom; Vm — Metastable Vacuum: a vacuum state can rewrite local physics. Course references included Abbott; higher-dimensional SF; Greg Egan — Schild's Ladder. The rule was strict: naming a work did not substitute for an explanation. They had to identify the mechanism that could migrate into another story and the consequences that could not be copied without remainder. Vela broke the first consensus. ‘If we can save the situation only by making the world resemble us more closely, we have not demonstrated the superiority of our solution. We have demonstrated only our power.’ Orin answered without raising their voice: ‘I do not want the perfect branch. I want us to know what we sacrificed in order to call it perfect.’ It was not a pedagogical quarrel. Over the last nights, the children’s differences had become incompatible political programs. Aster felt the Hunger precisely when an explanation closed too elegantly. A perfect theory reduced surprise, and surprise was the last symptom that something before her had not yet become part of her. 110 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS The children had noticed that their disagreement calmed her more than any extravagant universe did. Orin asked for a simulation of the option the group had just rejected. Aster gave him only the non-conscious model. He did not want to manufacture victims in order to validate his guilt; he wanted a map of absent costs. The distinction had become one of their working rules. The night did not end in victory. Orin learns that rescue by copying may be experienced by the rescued person as replacement. Aster recorded the decision in the world’s provenance register and, more importantly, allowed its inhabitants to contest it. For several eras she had been learning something that seems banal to lesser powers: technical reversibility is not the same as biographical reversibility. While Kesh closed the record, Tern compared the sector’s noise with the anomaly detected in the Vinge zone. The pattern reappeared, but only in worlds where Aster’s control weakened. The correlation was unpleasant: either someone was calling him from outside, or his own need for an outside was learning to forge evidence. For the course, Kesh also linked the night to the EXTENSION operator. In the Table, periodicity did not mean that the same objects reappeared, but that the same operation — adds a degree of freedom, capacity, or axis absent from the baseline world — could recur across different families. Thus a copy of a body, a copy of a mind, a copy of a world, and a copy of a history were not the same phenomenon, but they shared a conceptual chemistry. 111 Vela introduced the propagation test: if you remove the speculative idea and nothing in the institutions, relationships, or vocabulary has to be rewritten, the idea has remained scenery. Kesh introduced the opposite test: if the idea seems to explain every detail, you have overcompressed the world. Between the two tests lay the region in which an element became fertile without becoming superstition. Marae added the refusal test. Who can say “no,” and what happens afterward? In universes with near-divine technology, that question often separated an instrument from a regime. A power that treats refusal as a data error can be benevolent in intention and totalitarian in structure. They left without an oral summary. Aster had abandoned the habit of closing every night with a thesis; some worlds were more honestly preserved as problems than as lessons. 112 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS 113 PART 4​ TIME IS NOT A CORRIDOR A period in the curriculum of the five children 114 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS
